_comment: Findings known and accepted for this setup. A module that does not pass is still reported, but only counts as a regression if its result differs from 'result' here or it fails on a condition not listed under 'conditions'. Keyed by the module's name without the 'fapi2-security-profile-final-' prefix; 'conditions' are prefixes of the suite's condition names (the 'src' of its log entries), 'why' says why it is acceptable.

happy-flow.why: The suite checks the TLS cipher suites of the issuer's host. Through an ngrok tunnel that is ngrok's configuration, not Versola's; behind our own TLS termination it is checked for real.

ensure-holder-of-key-required.why: Same TLS cipher check as happy-flow.

test-claims-parameter-identity-claims.why: Skipped by the suite: it needs a claims configuration this plan does not provide.

refresh-token.why: The suite refreshes with a DPoP key other than the one the code was exchanged with; Versola holds a refresh token to the key it was issued to. RFC 9449 §5 requires that only of public clients, but the binding is what protects a native client behind edge, and nothing yet tells such a client from a web one. Deliberately not relaxed: versolauth/versola#728.

attempt-reuse-authorization-code-after-o.why: After a code is replayed Versola revokes the family and pushes the revocation to the client's back channel, but /userinfo keeps no record of revoked access tokens and still accepts the first one. Needs an auth-side revocation store: versolauth/versola#729.
